design.root_cause: Advanced Paste injects synthetic Ctrl/V input that the centralized runner hook ignores, but Keyboard Manager does not. The paste keystrokes therefore get remapped (for example Ctrl→Win or Ctrl→2), so the Advanced Paste window closes without sending a real paste sequence.
evidence: Issue #49663 provides a current repro on 0.100.2: remap Left Ctrl in Keyboard Manager, open Advanced Paste, choose an item, and nothing is pasted; remapping Ctrl to `2` even produces `2v`.
The issue includes a bug-report ZIP and a second concrete symptom (`2v` is typed) showing that Keyboard Manager is re-processing Advanced Paste's synthetic keystrokes.

In `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPasteModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp`, the injected `Ctrl` keydown/keyup events are sent without the Keyboard Manager injected flag, and the `V` events only carry `CENTRALIZED_KEYBOARD_HOOK_DONT_TRIGGER_FLAG`.
In `src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Helpers/ClipboardHelper.cs`, `SendSingleKeyboardInput` uses a private `0x5555` tag that Keyboard Manager never checks.

In `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp`, Keyboard Manager skips only events whose `dwExtraInfo` contains `CommonSharedConstants::KEYBOARDMANAGER_INJECTED_FLAG`.

affected_files.purpose: Injects the native Ctrl+V sequence for plain-text and direct-hotkey paste.
Injects the managed Ctrl+V sequence after the Advanced Paste UI chooses a format.
Filters PowerToys-generated keystrokes before they re-trigger global shortcuts.
Defines which injected events Keyboard Manager ignores during remap processing.
Existing UI automation coverage for paste actions; extend it with a Keyboard Manager remap regression.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The centralized hook ignores only events whose `dwExtraInfo` is exactly `CENTRALIZED_KEYBOARD_HOOK_DONT_TRIGGER_FLAG`.
implementation_steps.change: Treat the centralized-hook marker as a bitmask so one synthetic event can carry both the centralized marker and the Keyboard Manager injected flag.
edge_cases: Existing 0x110-tagged callers must keep working unchanged.
Do not broaden the check so far that unrelated third-party `dwExtraInfo` values are ignored accidentally.
tests: Regression-test an existing centralized-hook feature such as PowerAccent so its injected keys still bypass the runner hook.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The plain-text paste path releases modifiers and injects Ctrl+V, but those events either have no `dwExtraInfo` or only carry the centralized-hook marker, so Keyboard Manager reprocesses them.
implementation_steps.change: Tag every synthetic key event used for the paste sequence with a combined PowerToys-injected marker that includes `CommonSharedConstants::KEYBOARDMANAGER_INJECTED_FLAG`.
edge_cases: Injected modifier restores must keep their original left/right key identity.
Tag key-up events too, or Keyboard Manager can still mutate the release path and strand modifiers.
tests: Manual: with `Left Ctrl -> Left Win`, choose a clipboard item from Advanced Paste and confirm the target app receives paste content rather than the Start menu.
Manual: with `Left Ctrl -> 2`, confirm no literal `2v` is typed.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The managed paste path uses a private `0x5555` tag that the keyboard stack does not interpret as a PowerToys-injected event.
implementation_steps.change: Replace the ad-hoc constant with the same combined injected marker used by the native Advanced Paste path.
implementation_steps.code_block:
private const nuint AdvancedPasteInjectedTag = 0x111; // 0x110 centralized hook + 0x1 keyboard manager
...
dwExtraInfo = AdvancedPasteInjectedTag,
edge_cases: Keep the helper deterministic across x64 and Arm64 by using `nuint`/`UIntPtr` consistently.
The managed and native tags must stay in sync.
tests: Exercise both the plain-text hotkey path and the Advanced Paste UI selection path under the same Keyboard Manager remap.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Existing Advanced Paste UI tests verify ordinary Ctrl+1 / button-driven paste flows, but none enable a Keyboard Manager remap before invoking paste.
implementation_steps.change: Add a regression test that turns on a `Left Ctrl` remap, opens Advanced Paste, selects a paste option, and asserts the destination app receives pasted content rather than literal keystrokes.
edge_cases: The test must clean up the remap afterward.
Cover both keyboard selection and mouse-click selection because the issue repro mentions either path.
tests: Run the Advanced Paste UI test project with the new remap regression.

verify: Run the existing Advanced Paste UI test project after adding the Keyboard Manager remap regression.
Manual repro: map `Ctrl (Left)` to `Win (Left)`, open Advanced Paste, choose an item, and confirm the target app receives pasted text.
Manual repro: map `Ctrl (Left)` to `2`, choose an Advanced Paste item, and confirm no literal `2v` is typed into the target app.
risks: Changing the centralized-hook comparison from equality to bitmask must not accidentally ignore unrelated synthetic events.
If any injected key in the paste sequence is left untagged, mixed remap states can still strand modifiers or partially re-trigger Keyboard Manager.
alternatives: Temporarily disable Keyboard Manager while Advanced Paste is open. Rejected because it is global and race-prone.
Special-case Advanced Paste inside Keyboard Manager. Rejected because the injected-event flag already exists as the intended cross-module contract.
